name_reason: Compliant with data_fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> convention: domain=chapter, descriptor=ch17_end_scene_char_pos_y_table. 'ch17' is a real chapter ID (range 01-30), not an address residue. Name reflects the data type (a per-char position table). No Ghidra address residue suffix.
purpose: Per-character Y tile coordinate table for the chapter 17 (Blade of Blood and Ice / 血與冰之刃) end scene; supplies the pos_y array for placing chars 0..0xF on the battle map.
logic_summary: fd2_chapter_17_end (0x23b5f) copies all 16 bytes onto its stack via REP MOVSD x4 (ESI=0x521b3 @ 0x23b85) and passes the block as the pos_y argument to fd2_setup_chars_and_camera_for_intro (0x233c6). That setup helper loops char_idx 0..0xF and does runtime_char[char_idx].bPos_y = *(byte*)(char_idx + pos_y_base), i.e. indexes the table one byte per char (stride 1). Paired with the adjacent pos_x_table at 0x521a3 (copied immediately before at 0x23b77). Read-only.
element_semantics: Element [i] = Y tile coordinate placed into runtime_char[i].bPos_y for character index i (i=0..15). Values 0x12..0x15 (18..21) are map tile rows. Parallel to data_fd2_chapter_ch17_end_scene_char_pos_x_table[i] which supplies the X coordinate for the same char i.
notes: src comment block (chtab2.c lines 133-147) was already accurate, precise, and ASCII-clean; every claim (16-byte MOVSD x4 copy, pos_y arg, per-char byte index into runtime_char.bPos_y for chars 0..0xF, read-only flat uint8[16], adjacency to pos_x_table @ 0x521A3) was verified against disassembly of fd2_chapter_17_end and decompilation of fd2_setup_chars_and_camera_for_intro. No src edit needed. Ghidra side: the description previously sat in PRE_COMMENT (the abolished data-plate mechanism per project_ghidra_data_plate_mechanism); migrated it to PLATE_COMMENT via run_script_inline Java API and cleared the stale PRE_COMMENT (set_plate_via_java_api). is_const=true: only two xrefs (READ @ 0x23b8a + DATA @ 0x23b85), both reads from the same caller, zero writers. A Ghidra artifact sub-symbol 'chapter_17_end_event_arg_f' at 0x521b7 overlaps inside this 16-byte table (the 'Globals overlap smaller symbols' warning); it is not a separate object and the table extent is bounded at 16 bytes by pos_x_table sibling layout and the next real table at 0x521c3.
